name: Tata Consumer Products Ltd
title: Tata Consumer Products Ltd - 500800 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Consumer Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR5,349 crore, with EBITDA up 19% and margin at 13.6%, up 70 bps.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12% to INR5,349 crore (9% in constant currency), with India business UVG of 13%. EBITDA grew 19% and margin expanded 70 bps to 13.6%, while net profit rose 29% to INR427 crore (reported EPS INR4.31; adjusted EPS INR4.67). Growth businesses grew 47% and reached 36% of revenue, with Sampann, RTD and Capital Foods/Organic India leading. India tea revenue fell 4% despite 2% volume growth as tea prices were passed on, and India margins compressed sequentially on inflation, staggered pricing, higher A&P and FX losses.

segments.name: India salt
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% on 7% volume growth despite June price increase (Tata Salt orange bag MRP INR30 to INR32); value-added salt grew 13%; market share close to 39%.

segments.name: India tea and coffee
segments.commentary: Revenue down 4% to INR1,200 crore as tea prices were passed on; tea volume +2%, coffee +24%. Unusually long summer and LPG shortage hit small restaurants and tea stalls in the south.

segments.name: Sampann and growth portfolio
segments.commentary: Sampann revenue +58%, volume-led; core pulses/spices/poha/vermicelli growing about 30%, with cold-pressed oil and dry fruits adding to growth. Sampann margin up 150-200 bps YoY.

segments.name: RTD (water and beverages)
segments.commentary: Revenue +41% on 38% volume growth; Tata Water Plus volumes up 35% with revenue +41%. Kombucha Zero launched in two variants.

segments.name: Capital Foods and Organic India
segments.commentary: Capital Foods INR232 crore (+40%); Organic India INR118 crore (+27%); combined gross margin close to 50%. Tata Soulfull grew 45%.

segments.name: International (incl. Starbucks India)
segments.commentary: Constant currency +3%, reported +16%. US +7% constant currency (seventh straight quarter of share gains); UK and Canada hit by warm weather; Starbucks revenue +11%. Non-branded and solubles/plantation declined on lower coffee prices.

guidance_outlook: Growth portfolio (30%+ growth) guided at 30% plus; Capital Foods and Organic India aspiration 25-30% growth.
Salt growth target 5-7%; ambition to cross 40% salt share quickly.
Tea volume guidance mid-single digit in the short to medium term; tea input inflation of 7-10% planned for.
Starbucks India expected to deliver high single-digit top-line growth going forward.
Full-year EBITDA margin expansion guided at 50-70 bps; management expects operating leverage to kick in as headcount stays broadly flat.
Management reiterated double-digit consolidated revenue growth as the norm, with some quarters at mid-teens and others at low double digits.
Medium-term aspiration: good India food business at 17-20% EBITDA margin; tea and salt gross margin 33-36%.
capex_capacity: Water business: adding capacity for next season, and possibly for the following season, after underestimating demand in some regions.
Capital Foods noodles capacity now in place; Cup Noodles launched and chilli oil expanded; a Korean noodle launch is coming soon.
Most Organic India and Capital Foods production is in-house; RTD is run by dedicated co-packers; Sampann relies heavily on outsourcing.
Management is evaluating bringing scale categories in-house; manufacturing capex for these categories is described as not heavy.
Water distribution reach about 40-50% of the 75% of the country where it is available; North and West are described as white space.
demand_pricing: Tea: input cost inflation of 7-10% seen so far, mainly at the lower end of the portfolio; pricing taken in June, with more to follow if inflation persists; buying is still early.
Salt: calibrated price increase from June 1; price hikes expected to settle in about a quarter.
Coffee: lower coffee prices helped the branded US business; the non-branded business is pass-through, so management calls the net effect positive.
Pulses: management expects to pass on any price rise; Sampann pulses about INR600-700 crore in a INR2.2 lakh crore pulses market with 6% branded penetration.
Non-branded business was down 10% constant currency; solubles down 12% and plantation down 8%.
Management says it has gained market share in tea in relative terms over the last couple of years, although Nielsen disclosure has been stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Whether growth businesses can invest in own capacity, pass on cost inflation in spices, dry fruits and edible oil, and reach a 35% growth norm for Capital Foods and Organic India.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most Capital Foods and Organic India production is in-house, and inflation will be passed on with a time lag. It set the Capital Foods and Organic India norm at 25-30% growth, with the go-to-market reset completed in February.

qa_highlights.question: Why India margins fell sequentially while international margins rose.
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goenka cited input cost inflation, a timing gap between cost hikes and staggered pricing, higher A&P, and FX losses on hedges in India. International margins benefited from lower US coffee prices.

qa_highlights.question: Tea pricing outlook and inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil D'Souza said tea inflation is 7-10% so far, with buying still early; pricing will be reviewed after 15-30 days and taken up if needed to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of margin expansion beyond salt pricing, and the path toward a 20% margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers listed were full pricing impact, US coffee normalisation, cost saving drives, mix shift to Capital Foods and Organic India, water utilisation gains and operating leverage, with Sampann margins close to 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether Starbucks and tea growth can stay in double digits.
qa_highlights.answer: Starbucks same-store sales grew mid-single digit; with new stores, management expects high single-digit top-line growth. Tea volume is guided at mid-single digit.

risks_watch: Tea input inflation of 7-10% during peak cropping season, with pricing action needed to protect margins.
El Nino and erratic monsoon, plus lower pulse sowing, which could raise prices in pulses and tea.
Staggered pricing against upfront cost inflation (packaging, freight, fuel, dry fruits, spices), and West Asia-related cost volatility.
Coffee price normalisation affecting the non-branded business; FX losses on hedges.
Capital Foods and Organic India go-to-market still being built, with sales-rep vacancies and distributor gaps.
Sequential India margin compression: management says the Q1 India EBITDA margin dip is timing-related and expects it to recover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the growth portfolio, with clear targets, but cautious on tea pricing and near-term margins, which management attributes to timing and inflation. Management avoided forecasting tea prices and commodity moves and declined to commit to a fixed Nielsen-based market share figure.
key_quotes: Growth businesses grew 47% year-on-year and scaled to 36%. In terms of growth, I think this was the best ever quarter for the growth businesses for TCPL
So, we've guided for 50 bps to 70 bps margin expansion for the year, Mihir.
I've stopped trying to forecast tea completely. We will move in line with the market.
Yes, the answer to that question is 25% to 30% should be the new normal going forward.

growth.why: Management reiterates double-digit consolidated revenue growth as the norm, 30%+ growth for the growth portfolio, and 50-70 bps FY27 margin expansion; backing is partly specific (growth portfolio at 36% of revenue, salt price hikes, water capacity additions) but no quantified capacity or order book supports the full guidance.
